blogs.title: Semaglutide Sparks an Immune Storm — First Report Linking GLP‑1 Receptor Agonists With Necrotising Myopathy
blogs.description: This article walks through a novel case where a patient’s first dose of semaglutide led to progressive proximal weakness and a dramatic rise in creatine kinase over several months—a presentation compatible with immune‐mediated necrotising myopathy (IMNM). It examines putative mechanisms connecting GLP‑1 signalling to muscle autoimmunity, considers whether this reflects an idiosyncratic reaction or emerging class‐wide toxicity, and discusses practical implications for prescribing choices.

blogs.title: Beyond Fatty Liver – How To Tell Hepatic Transaminitis From Muscle Breakdown
blogs.description: Elevated AST±ALT frequently masks skeletal muscle injury when both organs release enzymes similarly following stressors—or medication exposure—in patients treated with glucagon-like peptide (IIA)s. This post explains a systematic lab workflow incorporating serial CK trends, symptom timing, bedside urinalysis findings, bedside MRI or biopsy clues that help avoid misattribution and prevent delays in diagnosing drug‑induced IMNM.

blogs.title: A Short Course Can Cure It All — Optimizing Steroids Plus IVIG For Acute IMNM
blogs.description: Despite historic thinking that lifelong immunosuppression is mandatory for most idiopathic IMNMs this case demonstrates powerful recovery achieved with 5 days methylprednisone pulse followed immediately by a brief two gram/kg IVIg regimen followed by relatively rapid steroid tapering off entirely within eight months. Detailed therapeutic rationale combined with literature review illustrates circumstances where aggressive early rescue translates into durable remission.

blogs.title: The Heart Screens For Smug Tremor — Cardiac Findings In Autoimmune Neuromuscular Disease
blogs.description: The patient’s transient dyspnoea was initially attributed solely to GI side effects yet cardiac workup revealed mid‐septal hypokinesis paired mildly elevated troponin and BNP suggestive humourous assault on myocardial tissue despite negative late gadolinium enhancement. This section dissects how inflammatory infiltrates outside skeletal muscles manifest clinically equivalently—as myocarditis—not unlike stress cardiomyopathy observations past seasonal virus triggers.
